title: Chole Bhature
steps: Soak chickpeas overnight, then boil with tea leaves for color.
Prepare a rich gravy with onion, tomato, ginger, garlic, and chole masala.
Simmer the boiled chickpeas in the gravy until thick and flavorful.
Prepare a dough of maida and sooji, and let it rest.
Roll into bhaturas and deep-fry in hot oil until puffed and golden.

fullIngredients.name: Chole masala, black cardamom, pomegranate seeds

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A Sunday breakfast and filling lunch favorite in Delhi .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Ask for extra onions and a green chilli on the side - it cuts through the richness perfectly .

title: Bedmi Puri with Aloo Sabzi
steps: Soak and coarsely grind the urad dal with ginger, chillies, and spices.
Knead wheat flour with the spiced dal mixture and a little oil into a dough.
Prepare a tangy aloo sabzi (potato curry) with tomatoes and cumin.
Roll the dough into small puris and deep-fry until crisp.
Serve hot puris alongside the spicy aloo sabzi.

fullIngredients.name: 1 cup dhuli urad dal (skinned black lentil)
Red chilli powder, dry mango powder

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The dough should be tight just like poori dough .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Double frying method ensures the poories fluff up properly .

title: Nihari
steps: Slow-cook mutton on the bone with whole spices, ginger-garlic, and chillies.
Allow it to simmer gently overnight or for several hours until very tender.
Prepare a slurry of wheat flour and water, and stir it into the gravy.
Cook until the gravy thickens and oil floats to the top.
Serve hot garnished with ginger juliennes and fresh coriander.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The nihari counters near Jama Masjid open before 7 AM and run out by mid morning .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Set an alarm - this is a breakfast-only affair.

title: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
steps: Marinate chicken in yogurt and spices, then roast or grill.
Prepare a rich makhani sauce using tomato puree, butter, and cream.
Season the sauce with kasuri methi, honey, and garam masala.
Add the cooked chicken to the sauce and simmer gently.
Serve hot, garnished with a swirl of cream.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The original version at Moti Mahal in Daryaganj is still the gold standard .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The dal makhani here is equally important, slow-cooked overnight with butter and cream .

title: Mughlai Kebabs (Seekh/Shami)
steps: Mix minced meat with finely chopped onion, ginger-garlic, and green chillies.
Season with garam masala, red chilli powder, and coriander.
Shape the mixture onto skewers (for seekh) or into patties (for shami).
Grill, pan-fry, or roast until cooked through and slightly charred.
Serve hot with mint chutney and onion rings.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Old Delhi areas around Jama Masjid are packed with kebab legends like Karim's and Qureshi Kebab Corner .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The smoky charcoal aroma is the hallmark of authentic Delhi kebabs.

title: Gol Gappa (Pani Puri)
steps: Prepare hollow wheat puris and lightly crack the top of each.
Stuff each puri with a little mashed potato and boiled chickpeas.
Prepare a spicy mint-coriander water and a sweet tamarind water.
Fill the stuffed puris with a mixture of both waters.
Serve immediately for a burst of flavor.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Ask for 'teekha paani' if you want the hot version .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Most vendors give you a sweet tamarind shot at the end - don't skip it .

tipsList.title: Tip 3
tipsList.desc: Best at Chandni Chowk, Rajouri Garden, Lajpat Nagar .

title: Aloo Tikki Chaat
steps: Mash boiled potatoes and form into flat patties (tikkis).
Shallow fry the tikkis on a hot tawa until very crisp and golden.
Place tikkis on a plate and crush them slightly.
Top with beaten yogurt, sweet tamarind chutney, and spicy green chutney.
Garnish with sev, raw onions, and chaat masala.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Bishan Swaroop at Chandni Chowk has been making just three dishes since 1923 - the aloo tikki is reason enough to visit .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Ask for 'loaded' - all toppings, no holding back .

title: Samosa
steps: Prepare a firm dough with maida, oil, and salt; let it rest.
Prepare a spiced filling of boiled potatoes, peas, cumin, and coriander.
Roll out the dough, cut into halves, and form into cones.
Stuff cones with the potato mixture and seal the edges tightly.
Deep-fry on low-medium heat until crisp and golden brown.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Delhi is widely regarded as the home of the perfect samosa.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best enjoyed with chai, especially on rainy evenings .

title: Momos (Steamed Dumplings)
steps: Prepare a smooth dough of wheat flour and water.
Finely chop cabbage, onion, and carrots; mix with ginger, garlic, and soy sauce.
Roll dough into thin circles and place a spoonful of filling in the center.
Pleat and seal the edges to form dumplings.
Steam for 10-12 minutes until cooked and serve with spicy red chutney.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Lajpat Nagar, Amar Colony, Majnu Ka Tila are popular momo destinations .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Dolma Aunty Momos and Hunger Strike have become cult favourites .

tipsList.title: Tip 3
tipsList.desc: Momos at Rs 60-100 a plate make them one of the best value local food options .

title: Dahi Bhalla
steps: Soak urad dal, grind to a fluffy batter, and deep-fry into round bhallas.
Soak the fried bhallas in warm water until soft, then squeeze out excess water.
Place bhallas on a plate and cover completely with thick beaten yogurt.
Drizzle with sweet tamarind chutney and spicy green chutney.
Sprinkle with roasted cumin powder, black salt, and coriander.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Natraj Dahi Bhalla Corner in Chandni Chowk is a long-time favourite .

title: Parathas (Stuffed Flatbread)
steps: Prepare a soft dough of whole wheat flour and let it rest.
Prepare a spiced stuffing (potato, paneer, or mixed vegetables).
Roll a small portion of dough, place the stuffing in the center, and seal.
Roll out gently into a flatbread.
Cook on a hot tawa with generous amounts of ghee or butter until golden and crisp.

fullIngredients.name: Stuffing (potato, paneer, gobhi, or mixed vegetables)

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Parathe Wali Gali in Chandni Chowk has been frying parathas for over a century .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: PT Gaya Prashad Shiv Charan is among the oldest surviving shops .

tipsList.title: Tip 3
tipsList.desc: Come hungry. Order two - one savoury, one sweet .

title: Jalebi
steps: Prepare a fermented batter of maida and water.
Prepare a warm sugar syrup flavored with cardamom.
Pipe the batter into hot ghee in a spiral shape.
Fry until crisp and golden brown on both sides.
Immediately soak the fried jalebis in the warm syrup for a few minutes.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Old Famous Jalebi Wala at Dariba Kalan fries them in pure desi ghee .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Pair your jalebi with a glass of rabri (thickened, sweetened milk) - non-negotiable .

title: Ram Ladoo
steps: Soak moong dal, chana dal, and urad dal for a few hours.
Grind into a coarse, fluffy batter with ginger and green chillies.
Deep-fry small spoonfuls of batter until golden and crisp.
Grate radish and mix with radish leaves and lemon juice.
Serve the hot ladoos topped with grated radish and tangy green chutney.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A popular Delhi street snack, especially in winter .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best eaten fresh and hot from the fryer.

title: Kulfi
steps: Reduce full cream milk on a slow flame until thickened and rich.
Stir in sugar, cardamom powder, and rose water.
Add chopped nuts (almonds, pistachios) and mix well.
Pour the mixture into kulfi molds and freeze until set.
Unmold and serve cold, optionally with falooda.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The kulfi counters near Chandni Chowk and the old kulfiwala near Gali Paranthe Wali are the ones to find .

title: Kachori
steps: Prepare a stiff dough with wheat flour and oil.
Prepare a spiced filling using dal or peas, onion, ginger, and spices.
Stuff small portions of dough with the filling and flatten slightly.
Deep-fry on a very low flame until thoroughly crisp and golden.
Serve hot with spicy potato curry or chutneys.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Matar (pea) kachori and pyaz (onion) kachori are especially popular in Delhi .
